newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with traders sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said on Monday.
U.S. financial markets are closed today for the President's day holiday.
"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments. There wasn't much activity today due to a shortage of players because of the holiday in the U.S.," a local dealer said.
"But some people are waiting Wednesday's release of the (January) consumer price index (CPI) and (U.S.) international trade data (for December), for more clues to market direction," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday was unchanged from last Friday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent but week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from last Friday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
